title: (tatiya) nibbānapaṭisaṃyutta sutta
credit: Pāḷi text and English translation as in Mor’s Pāḷi Workshop booklet.

paras.en: Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now on that occasion the Blessed One was instructing, inspiring, uplifting, and gladdening the bhikkhus with a Dhamma talk connected with nibbāna. And those bhikkhus were listening to the Dhamma with eager ears, attending to it as a matter of vital concern, applying their whole mind to it.
Then, realizing the significance of this, the Blessed One on that occasion uttered this inspired utterance:

“There is, bhikkhus, the unborn, unbecome, unmade, unconditioned. If, bhikkhus, there were no unborn, unbecome, unmade, unconditioned, no escape would be discerned here from the born, become, made, conditioned.
But because there is an unborn, unbecome, unmade, unconditioned, an escape is discerned from the born, become, made, conditioned.”
